utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Norwalk' by name among the cities in its service area.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Clean Power Alliance's own homepage states it serves '38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties' and names each one individually via its site's community directory; Norwalk is not among the named communities. No other Los Angeles/Ventura County CCA serving Norwalk was found, so Southern California Edison (SCE) is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

county.notes: Norwalk is a well-documented Los Angeles County city; also listed under Los Angeles County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of Norwalk Community Development Department
permit_authority.notes: Both norwalkca.gov and ci.norwalk.ca.us returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session. This department name is confirmed via search-engine indexing of the city's own page title, but the SolarAPP+ page's specific content (eligibility, fees, timeline, contacts) could not be independently verified.

permit_url.notes: URL identified via search-engine indexing; norwalkca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, so its content could not be independently read or verified.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Norwalk/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Application form furnished by the Building Official, per the standard plan and checklist published on the City's website
Verification that the support structure can transfer all wind, seismic, dead, and live loads to the building foundation (standard engineering evaluation techniques)

Verification that the existing electrical system (line, load, ground, bonding wiring, panel/subpanel sizes) is adequately sized to carry the new photovoltaic electrical loads (standard electrical inspection techniques)

value: Only one inspection shall be required and performed by the Building Official for eligible small residential rooftop solar energy systems, done in a timely manner and may include a consolidated inspection by the Building Official and Fire Chief
If the system fails inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized

timeline_days.notes: Norwalk Municipal Code Section 15.52.060(B) states the Building Official shall administratively approve a complete application and issue permits, but states no explicit day-count turnaround figure.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Norwalk Municipal Code Section 15.52.020 defines 'small residential rooftop solar energy systems' by direct reference to Government Code Section 65850.5(j)(3) rather than restating specific numeric size caps or dwelling-type limits in the ordinance text itself, so no eligibility_constraints figures are recorded here.
